summary: Lexy, staying at Mrs. Royce's house, watches Captain Grey walk off in the rain, comparing him unfavorably in her thoughts to Mr. Houseman, whom she has met only briefly and who wrote her a stiff, offended letter. Mrs. Royce, who believes Lexy is a writer, sets up the sewing room as a writing space and leaves her alone there. Lexy, who had falsely claimed to be a writer the night before, sits down to write a letter to Mr. Houseman telling him what she knows about Caroline's disappearance.
one_line: Lexy, hosted by Mrs. Royce and pretending to be a writer, thinks fondly of Mr. Houseman and writes him about Caroline's disappearance.
key_facts: Captain Grey strides off up the muddy road in the rain, looking curiously elegant in his wet weather clothes.
Lexy thinks Captain Grey is awfully nice and awfully handsome and believes he is absolutely trustworthy and honorable.
Lexy had talked with Mr. Houseman for five or ten minutes in the park, and his conversation was entirely about Caroline Enderby.
Mr. Houseman is described as quick-tempered and sadly lacking in patience.
Mr. Houseman wrote Lexy a stiff, offended, boyish letter and then disappeared.
Lexy hopes very much to see Mr. Houseman again, though she has no sensible reason to.
Mrs. Royce believes Lexy is a writer and says she has fixed up the sewing room for her writing.
Lexy had told a shocking falsehood the night before by claiming to be a writer.
Mrs. Royce has put a nice strong table with drawers in the sewing room for Lexy's papers.
Lexy calls Mrs. Royce a dear, saying so because she thinks it and liking people makes her tell them so.
Mrs. Royce says her cousin's husband was writing for the movies and became upset when disturbed.
Mrs. Royce shuts Lexy in the small upstairs room to work.
Lexy finds it easy to write letters because she writes only when she has something to say.
Lexy decides to use the time to write to Mr. Houseman and tell him all she knows about Caroline's disappearance.
